# Expected output SHAPE for s02 (the streaming XML message parser).
#
# The parser is deterministic — there is no LLM here, just a hard-coded sample
# assistant turn fed in chunks. So unlike s01 this output is reproducible.
#
# `go run .` (default: feed the sample in 7-byte chunks, which splits tags
# across chunk boundaries on purpose) prints to stderr+stdout:
#
#   [s02] feeding 39 chunk(s) of a streamed assistant message
#   === final parse ===
#     [0] text: "I'll create a small greeter for you."
#     [1] tool_use: write_to_file
#           path = "greet.go"
#           content = "package main\n\nimport \"fmt\"\n\n// prints a greeting. ..."
#     [2] text (partial): "That file is ready."
#
# What to verify you ran it correctly:
#   1. Block [0] is a TEXT block (the prose before the tool tag).
#   2. Block [1] is a TOOL_USE block named write_to_file, with BOTH params
#      (path and content) extracted — even though the chunking split the tags.
#   3. The content param survived its multi-line body verbatim (the
#      lastIndexOf(</content>) recovery path).
#   4. Block [2] is TEXT and marked "(partial)": trailing text is always partial
#      because the stream could continue.
#
# `go run . -steps` prints the parse after EACH chunk so you can watch the tool
# block start as partial and become complete once </write_to_file> arrives.
#
# `go run . -chunk 0` feeds the whole sample at once; the FINAL parse is byte-for
# -byte identical to the chunked run — that equivalence is the streaming
# guarantee (see TestByteByByteEqualsAllAtOnce).
